finding_feedback.rationale: The checkpoint Ready cutover is resolved by separating server readiness from interaction admission and draining pre-cutover control interactions before opening the interaction gate.

findings.observation: The corrected active lifecycle uses a biased select with children.observe_raw ahead of both realtime.next_event and the heartbeat tick. A continuously ready PlayerState lane is therefore always selected; update_state uses a coalescing watch and can keep succeeding, so the loop has no per-source budget that forces the overdue heartbeat or realtime terminal branch to run. The checkpoint Ready cutover repeats this pattern with control.receive ahead of realtime.next_event and an always-ready activation branch, and it has no heartbeat branch at all.
findings.impact: A high-rate authenticated control producer can starve lease heartbeats, server Ready/terminal observation, and checkpoint-cutover completion. The launcher may keep an active WebSocket past its locally maintained lease cadence or fail to notice a terminal realtime task promptly, violating the contract's heartbeat-liveness and fail-closed teardown boundaries and enabling a local denial of service.
findings.recommendation: Replace the unbounded biased control preference with explicit bounded draining or a fair arbitration scheme that still defines the Ready interaction watermark. Ensure overdue heartbeat and completed realtime task checks preempt further control-state work, and add deterministic continuously-ready PlayerState regressions proving heartbeat execution, Ready/terminal observation, and bounded cutover completion.
